4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The hypothesis program ([slate](2026-09-07-hypothesis-program.md)) promised that every experiment would end with a verdict and an interval recorded under `data/proving-ground/`, and that a refutation would be recorded with the same care as a confirmation. Two days of runs on the operator's Claude Code subscription produced thirty records and eleven folds; nothing summarizes them, so a reader who wants to know whether the harness loop beats the product's own loop, whether a smaller model is worse, whether the directive loop earns its attempts, whether a knowledge pack changes anything, and what a router could gain has to read the proving-ground README end to end. This note is that summary, with the refutations first and the noise floor stated before any delta.
10	
11	## Proposal
12	
13	Read the records as follows, adopt the readings as the current state of knowledge about this harness on these tasks, and queue the slices the results demand rather than any change the results do not support.
14	
15	### The instrument, and what it can tell apart
16	
17	Every number below comes from a frozen paired experiment or a fleet run on `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in tiers 2 to 4 plus ten tier-5 tasks whose hidden cases the validator holds, eight of them audited so that every hidden case is derivable from the prompt. A cell is one task, one repetition, one arm; the runner validates the workspace against the task's checks after each attempt, issues a directive clustered by failing channel, and certifies when every case passes. Since 09:25 UTC on 2026-09-08 every cell is sealed: bubblewrap mounts an empty parent over the run directory with only the cell's workspace bound back in, the read barrier denies the parent and grants the workspace, and reads the barrier refuses are counted on the run. Two facts about the instrument bound every reading:
18	
19	- **The noise floor is one flip in sixteen.** The middle product model ran the same sixteen sealed tier-5 cells twice at seed 2 (the twentieth and twenty-first records); the runs agree on fifteen cells ([fold](../../../../data/proving-ground/folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json)). Against an unsealed run of the same arm the agreement is fourteen and thirteen of sixteen, with one task (conf-canon) certified twice in both sealed runs and never in the unsealed one. A paired delta of 0.0625 on sixteen cells is inside one arm's own run-to-run variation; a delta has to be three flips wide before it says anything.
20	- **The arms of every recorded experiment ran one after the other, not interleaved.** The experiments service ran the whole baseline arm and then the whole candidate arm, so an arm of these records is confounded with its hour on the shared subscription. Seed pairing does not remove this. The cell-interleaved schedule is the slice below.
21	
22	### What was measured
23	
24	| Experiment | Tier, cells | Arms | Certified | Delta, interval, verdict | What separates the arms |
25	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26	| E2 harness loop vs product loop | 3, 36 | route vs delegated product, same model | 18 of 18 vs 18 of 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | wall time level (harness faster in 11 of 18 pairs, medians 164 vs 179 s); harness spend write-dominant before session continuity (3,005,288 cache-write tokens over 200 queries) |
27	| E2 as two fleets | 2 and 4, 12 + 18 each | same | 30 of 30 vs 30 of 30 | fleets, not folded | harness faster on tier 2 (9 of 12 pairs), slower on tier 4 (6 of 18 pairs, 2,915 vs 2,292 s of cell time) |
28	| E2 on tier 5, unsealed | 5, 32 | same, audited tasks, seed 2 | 12 of 16 vs 11 of 16 | −0.0625, [−0.125, 0], inconclusive | inside the noise floor; the product arm ran uncapped and its misses cost up to 3,459 s and 5.60 USD each |
29	| E2 on tier 5, sealed, capped | 5, 32 | same, same caps on both arms, continuity | 15 of 16 vs 14 of 16 | −0.0625, [−0.125, 0], inconclusive | one flip, inside the noise floor; the product's two misses each breached a cap after one attempt; harness faster in 15 of 16 pairs (5,740 vs 8,187 s) and cheaper (7,695,132 vs 25,817,220 billed tokens) |
30	| E1 small vs middle | 3, 36 | sonnet vs haiku | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | small model 405 steps vs 182, 6,719 vs 3,807 s, 844,538 vs 358,054 output tokens |
31	| E1 middle vs large | 3, 36 | sonnet vs opus | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive | large model 156 steps vs 208, 2,070 vs 3,948 s, 166,606 vs 367,172 output tokens |
32	| E1 middle vs large, sealed | 5, 32 | sonnet vs opus, seed 2 | 13 vs 16 | 0.1875, [0.125, 0.25], promote | large model first-attempt on every cell; 164 steps vs 267, 3,572 vs 7,451 s, 189,169 vs 561,271 output tokens |
33	| E1 small vs middle, sealed | 5, 32 | sonnet vs haiku, seed 2 | 14 vs 1 | −0.8125, [−0.875, −0.75], reject | small model spent all three attempts on fifteen cells; 604 steps vs 262, 11,227 vs 6,337 s, 736,856 vs 481,591 output tokens |
34	| E3 attempts, tier 3 | 3, 18 + 18 | three attempts vs one | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], fold says nothing | no cell used a second attempt |
35	| E3 attempts, tier 5 counterfactual | 5, 16 re-read | three vs one, from one run each | harness 11 vs 8; product 11 vs 11 | −0.1875, [−0.25, −0.125], reject for the cap; product 0 | the product loop's later attempts were a fresh child with the directive alone |
36	| E3 attempts, tier 5 paired | 5, 32 | three-rung vs one-rung ladder, same model | 15 of 16 vs 9 of 16 | −0.375, [−0.5625, −0.1875], reject for the cap of one | three certificates at a second attempt after a directive; the other three are first-attempt variation the loop absorbs (first attempts disagree on 9 of 16 cells between the arms); the later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells |
37	| E4 knowledge pack | 3, 18 + 18 | 2026-q3 pack mounted vs none | 18 vs 18 | 0, [0, 0], null | the pack was never opened: no skill call in any cell |
38	| E4 craft skills | 5, 16 folded against four sealed middle-model arms | three task-relevant skills mounted vs none | 13 of 16 vs 14, 13, 15, 15 of 16 | −0.0625, 0, −0.125, −0.125; every interval touches zero; inconclusive four times | every cell read all three skills; no certificate added, one task missed that no baseline missed; cache-write above every baseline |
39	| E5 downshift | 5, 32 | opus on three rungs vs opus then haiku, haiku, transcript kept | 16 vs 16 | 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction | the largest model certified every cell at the first attempt in both arms, so the downshift rung never ran; two runs of one arm put the cost noise floor under 7 percent in output tokens and 15 percent in cell time |

# @deepseek-ai/dsh-observatory

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The public page, folded from the persisted logs and nothing else. `ctx.observatory.snapshot()` folds the scoreboard through the scorekeeper over every persisted session, withholds the configured districts and the held-out split from its public rows while counting what it dropped, and records when it folded and how new its newest session is. `render(snapshot, now)` turns one snapshot into a self-contained HTML page and the same publication as JSON, and shows the staleness notice in place of every figure once the fold is too old. The service writes no session event. The [observatory Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-observatory.md) owns the design rationale, and the [Village note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) owns the publication rules it enforces.

content.content:
### Routing, E5, and what the ladder makes possible

The attempt ladder lets an arm name a model per attempt and the transcript interface of the hand-off, and E5 ran on it as three readings. The downshift never happened: the largest model certified every cell at its first rung in both arms, so the cheap rung it was to hand down to never ran, and the experiment measures only the cost noise floor of one arm run twice. The handoff tax is real: the cheap-first ladder with the transcript kept recovered 12 of the 14 certificates the smallest model misses, cost 2.5 times the strong model alone, and lost two certificates the strong model never loses from a clean start. The drop reading was the one result in a harness mechanism's favour, and it did not replicate: the same ladder with a fresh in-process child per rung, so the strong model inherits the workspace and the directive but not the cheap model's transcript, certified 14 of 16 against 11 with the transcript kept as an offline fold of two arms run an hour apart (the frozen pair had lost its candidate arm to a composition defect: the overlay patched an entry the base never names, which the include plugin skipped with a warning nothing printed), three flips all one way and all on the hardest tasks, 0.1875 with an interval of [0.0625, 0.3125]; run as one frozen pair on the fixed overlay on 2026-09-18 and cut by a container restart at 25 of 32 cells, it read 5 of 7 against 7 of 7 on its complete pairs, −0.2857, [−0.5714, 0], inconclusive, and on build-schedule and conf-canon, two of the fold's three flip tasks, the kept transcript certified both repetitions while the fresh child certified one each ([the record](../../../../data/proving-ground/README.md), [the fold](../../../../data/proving-ground/folds/2026-09-18-e5-drop-frozen-spawn-against-route-t5.json)). Where the fresh child missed, in both readings, the cheap rung alone had spent the cell's token cap before the strong rung ran, which is a budget allocation defect of the ladder, not a transcript effect. On these cells raw escalation still cannot beat starting strong on cost, so what the ladder buys is a cheaper answer on the cells the cheap model can do (2 of 16 here) at a higher total cost on the rest. A per-turn router in the style of Fugu is not tested by any of this and is not proposed.

## Slices the results demand
=== SLICES ===
## Slices the results demand

- **Interleave the arms** ([note](../../implemented/architecture/2026-09-18-interleaved-experiment-arms.md)): the experiments service schedules cells pairwise (baseline then candidate of the same cell, alternating) so an arm is not confounded with its hour. The digest and the fold are unchanged.
- **Finish the frozen drop pair with the share on the spawn arm.** The frozen pair on the fixed overlay ran 25 of its 32 cells before a container restart killed the driver; each ladder rung now takes its own share of the cell's caps, so the pair runs again with the cheap rung bounded on both arms, the nine candidate cells it never ran included, before anything is read from the drop.
- **A harder tier or more cells before any harness promotion.** Sixteen cells cannot show a harness effect smaller than 0.19; the next paired harness experiment runs four repetitions or sixteen tasks, and the tier-5 tasks that every model certifies at the first attempt (five of eight for the middle model) do not discriminate.
- **Program workflow integrity** ([note](2026-09-08-program-workflow-integrity.md)): a department certifies only a committed tree, the integration runs confined, an interrupted integration resumes.
- **The process claim over the route**: the census attributes the route's own product spawn to the route so a route cell can claim `process` isolation (task 85).

## Alternatives considered

content.content:
### What was supported

- **The largest product model beats the middle one on tier 5.** The one promotion-level verdict from a frozen pair: 16 of 16 against 13, 0.1875, [0.125, 0.25], the largest model first-attempt on every cell and cheaper on every measure. It ranks a model tier, not the harness.
- **Dropping the cheap model's transcript at the hand-off beats keeping it: not replicated.** The offline fold read 14 of 16 against 11 on the same ladder, 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], three flips all one way and all on the hardest tasks, from two arms run an hour apart on a shared subscription; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay, cut by a container restart at 25 of 32 cells, read 5 of 7 against 7 of 7 on its complete pairs, −0.2857, [−0.5714, 0], inconclusive, with two of the fold's three flip tasks flipping the other way. Both readings' fresh-child misses are cells whose cheap rung alone spent the token cap; nothing is promoted on the drop, and the pair's remaining cells are queued with the per-rung share on the spawn arm.

### What stayed inconclusive, and why
=== E5 drop rows ===
41:| E5 drop | 5, 16 + 16 folded, then 16 + 7 frozen (partial) | haiku then opus, opus with the transcript kept (route) vs the same ladder with a fresh in-process child per rung (spawn): folded offline after the frozen pair lost its candidate arm, then run as one frozen pair on the fixed overlay, which a container restart cut at 25 of 32 cells | 11 of 16 vs 14 of 16 folded; 7 of 7 vs 5 of 7 frozen | 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], promote as an offline fold; −0.2857, [−0.5714, 0], inconclusive on the seven frozen pairs | the offline fold's three flips toward the fresh child were on the hardest tasks; on two of those tasks the frozen pair flipped the other way, the kept transcript certifying both repetitions and the fresh child one each; in both readings every fresh-child miss is a cell whose cheap rung alone spent the token cap before the strong rung ran, the allocation defect the per-rung share closes; the nine candidate cells that never ran are queued |
=== updated stayed-inconclusive ===
### What stayed inconclusive, and why

Tiers 2 to 4 are saturated on certificates for all three product models under both loops, so every comparison there is inconclusive by construction and the information lives in steps, wall time, and spend. Tier 5 separates models completely and loops not at all; sixteen cells give an interval no narrower than ±0.19 for a real difference, and the noise floor is 0.0625. The bench can promote a model tier and it can refute; no frozen pair has promoted a harness change, the one harness mechanism with a promotion-level reading (the fresh child per rung) has it from an offline fold, and every harness change that landed this week (native tools, continuity, parity, the seal, the ladder) landed because a run showed a defect, not because an experiment showed a gain. The number to quote for the harness loop on the middle model is the held-out estimate: 15 of 16 with every certificate at the first attempt on eight environments nothing in the program had touched ([record](../../../../data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-bench-held-out-sonnet-all/manifest.json)), with the caveat that six of the eight are tier 2 or 3 and the two tier-5 tasks read 3 of 4.
